correctness.rationale: With \(e_k=x_k-x_\star\) and \(s_k=L\gamma_k\), the assumptions imply \(J^2=-I\), \(\widehat e_k=(I-s_kJ)e_k\), and \(F(\widehat x_k)=L(J+s_kI)e_k\). Direct inner-product evaluation yields \(\alpha_k=\gamma_k/(1+s_k^2)\), hence \(e_{k+1}=(I-s_kJ)e_k/(1+s_k^2)\). Orthogonality gives the exact norm factor \((1+s_k^2)^{-1/2}\). The critical-condition ratio is exactly \(s_k\). Under \(s_k\le A\), comparison of \(\log(1+s_k^2)\) with \(s_k^2\) proves the stated if-and-only-if convergence criterion. The packaged exact-rational checker replays the step and product identities on canonical blocks.

value.rationale: The claim gives a complete trajectory law on a canonical rotational monotone class explicitly used to motivate extragradient. It separates generic sublinear theory from the exact behavior of a maximally rotational, non-strongly-monotone benchmark and yields the sharp step-sequence boundary \(\sum_k(L\gamma_k)^2=\infty\). In particular, it shows that a decreasing schedule can be nonsummable yet fail to converge if it is square-summable, while every constant critical-condition step converges linearly with a known exact factor. This is a structurally motivated benchmark and convergence boundary, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a numerical recomputation.
